headline: Rockstar releases 27-minute GTA VI extended look on YouTube, showing PS5 footage
summary: The nearly 27-minute preview, featuring PS5 footage, emphasizes atmosphere and protagonists, feeling more like a movie than a game trailer. GTA VI launches November 19th for $79.99.
details: Rockstar has officially published its 'extended look' at Grand Theft Auto VI on YouTube, as promised. The nearly 27-minute preview initially premiered on Netflix, but was available on YouTube via creators before Rockstar's official upload.

The in-depth preview, featuring footage from the PS5 version, largely focuses on atmosphere, protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and highlighting game locations. It feels more like slices of a movie than a video game trailer, though some sections show playable shootouts, police car chases, basketball, and scuba diving.
Grand Theft Auto VI is set to release on November 19th. The game will have a starting price of $79.99.
caption:
The 27-minute GTA VI 'extended look' is out, offering a cinematic deep dive into the game's world and characters.

Rockstar has officially published its 'extended look' at Grand Theft Auto VI on YouTube, as promised. The nearly 27-minute preview initially premiered on Netflix, but was available on YouTube via creators before Rockstar's official upload.

The in-depth preview, featuring footage from the PS5 version, largely focuses on atmosphere, protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and highlighting game locations. It feels more like slices of a movie than a video game trailer, though some sections show playable shootouts, police car chases, basketball, and scuba diving.

Grand Theft Auto VI is set to release on November 19th. The game will have a starting price of $79.99.

Source: The Verge

headline_marked: [[Attackers using GitHub repositories]] as malware staging mechanisms, affecting nearly 1M devices
headline: Attackers using GitHub repositories as malware staging mechanisms, affecting nearly 1M devices
summary: Recent campaigns have affected nearly one million devices, with attackers creating hundreds of malicious repositories. This exploits the inherent trust developers place in GitHub's infrastructure.
details: GitHub, a backbone of modern software development, has become an irresistible target for cybercriminals. Threat actors are now weaponizing its infrastructure to distribute malware on an unprecedented scale.

Recent investigations have uncovered campaigns affecting nearly one million devices, with attackers creating hundreds of malicious repositories. Microsoft's analysis of the Storm-0409 malvertising campaign alone infected close to one million devices worldwide.

These are not random attacks; they are well-orchestrated, long-term campaigns that exploit fundamental assumptions about code repository security. Security researchers have identified over 1,300 GitHub repositories vulnerable to RepoJacking attacks.

The GitVenom campaign, for example, involved attackers creating hundreds of carefully crafted, legitimate-looking repositories over several years. These featured professionally written READMEs and realistic commit histories, often offering tools for Instagram automation or game hacking utilities.

The financial impact is significant, with researchers finding evidence of approximately five Bitcoin (worth about US $440,000) sent to attacker wallets. Trend Micro also uncovered abuse of GitHub’s release mechanism to host and distribute Lumma Stealer and other malware.

Attackers gravitate toward GitHub due to its unique combination of implied trust, accessibility, and technical features. Developers often assume GitHub URLs are legitimate, a trust that extends to automated systems and CI/CD pipelines.

GitHub's free hosting, content delivery network (CDN) capabilities, and version control features inadvertently benefit malicious actors. The Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) model further makes GitHub-based attacks economically attractive, eliminating the need for attackers to maintain their own command and control servers.
